text: Jamie Wrenly is a human witch. They are played by Taliesin Jaffe.
is an apparently human member of the Cerberus Assembly, who is in reality a doppelganger. She has been mentioned but not yet appeared in Critical Role.
is a human sorcerer and a member of Bells Hells. She is played by Laura Bailey.
Kagaronks are dangerous massive burrowing creatures that tunnel beneath the badlands of the Hellcatch Valley in Marquet.

, also known simply as Elder Abaddina, is a soothsayer and spiritual leader in Hearthdell, a village in Issylra. She lives in the Knotburrow, a cottage in the Arklune Fields covered in vibrant vegetation. As an NPC, Elder Abaddina is played by Matthew Mercer.
Lillith Anioska Daturai is a tiefling wizard, specializing in the School of Illusion. Lillith is the cousin of Zahra and an ally of Vox Machina. She is played by Kit Buss.
Martinet Ludinus Da'leth is an elven mage and the former leader of the Cerberus Assembly, having been alive at the time of its founding. As an NPC, Ludinus Da'leth was played by Matthew Mercer.

Lythir VaSuun is a drow mage of the Kryn Dynasty. While leading an ambush against the Muck Men in the Ashkeeper Peaks, Lythir and his war party engaged in battle with the adventuring party known as the Mighty Nein. As an NPC, Lythir is played by Matthew Mercer.
Kay Clearsight is a spellcaster, general, and commander of the Tide Regiment, one of the four Daxio Outrider regiments stationed at Fort Daxio in the Republic of Tal'Dorei.
is an elven wizard who served as Architect Arcane of the city of Avalir. She is played by Aabria Iyengar.
Lanata is a dryad of the Wildmother and, along with her sister Robur, the caretaker of the oak forest surrounding the Emerald Loop Caravan Stop in Xhorhas.
is the Dean of the Throne of Necromancy in Avalir, and a member of the Octothurge and the Ring of Silver. As an NPC in Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.
Enchantress Lornië was a spellcaster that worked with the Dev-Yat Mahiyi Colleges, and one of those responsible for leaving the Somnovem in oblivion for centuries after the Divergence.

Sunbreaker Olomon is the minotaur leader of Urzin and a warrior in the Kryn Dynasty army. An early follower of Leylas Kryn, he lived multiple lifetimes through consecution and is considered a paragon within the Dynasty. His current life as a minotaur allows him to fight the Dwendalian Empire on the front lines of battle. As an NPC, Olomon is played by Matthew Mercer.

Mynarc Furdahl is an undead warlock of Asmodeus living on the island of Kaltsel, on Eiselcross. Mynarc is willing to make deals in exchange for souls, on behalf of the archdevil. Mynarc has only been mentioned in the Explorer's Guide to Wildemount.
This unnamed individual, informally known as the Nonagon mage, was a spellcaster who explored the ruins of Aeor and was first contacted by the Somnovem.
, the Sister of Mists, was an angel of death who acted as a psychopomp for the souls of halflings in Aramán in connection with Rauwyn, the goddess of trickery and of the halflings.
Opash was a sanctioned necromancer who lived in Marquet during the Age of Arcanum.

Lord Preston Drodelon () is a former lord of the Quadroads in Vasselheim, Issylra. He is apparently the man encountered by Grog Strongjaw in the Quadroads district who was persuaded to draw one card from the Deck of Many Things; the man was granted the ability to cast the Wish spell twice and promptly used his first Wish to become "a powerful lord of the Quadroads". Because he left without giving Grog his name, he became known among the cast simply as the "Lord of the Quadroads". As an NPC, he is played by Matthew Mercer. He is also played by John Madison in .
is a gnomish construct specialist and a member of the Arcana Pansophical.
Oluk Wagonsbane is an infamous cyclops stormcaller and raider. So far, he has not appeared nor been mentioned onstream.
(pronounced [ˈpeɪʃə pɔɹˈkoʊ]) is an elven wizard who serves as Keeper of Scrolls and Archmage of the Librarium Incantatum in the city of Avalir. She is played by Marisha Ray.
Putridius Festerkin, also known as the Timberblight, is a dark druid revenant and a former member of the Slayer's Take. As an NPC, he is played by Nick Williams.
is a priestess of the Scaled Tyrant and leader of the Cult of the Caustic Heart.
Shaktia is a male djinni soldier from the Elemental Plane of Air who took up residence around Zephrah.
was a kobold paladin of the Platinum Dragon who defended Vasselheim during the Calamity. As an NPC, is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.
is an elf-orc Archivist of the Cobalt Soul in their Reserve in Westruun.

is an argonian necromancer who serves as waiter at the Dreary Jug (later renamed Grelnok's Skull), which he owns collectively with Grelnok, Hoa, Mallory, and Tavima. He is played by Sam Riegel in the Elder Scrolls Online: Blackwood trilogy.
Sorrowsworn are monstrosities personifying different aspects of despair, and can invoke these emotions in their targets to weaken them as part of their attacks.

Succubi and incubi are shapeshifting fiends who delight in the corruption of mortals through temptation. They are the same race, but when female-presenting they are called a succubus and when male-presenting an incubus.
Tarvis was a half-orc assassin and a member of the Clasp. He was played by Travis Willingham in .
is a gnome lycanthrope living in Barinak. As an NPC, Tarad is played by Matthew Mercer.

Ioun, the Knowing Mentor, also known as the Knowing Mistress, is the goddess of knowledge, prophecy, and skill. She opposes Vecna, who deals in dark secrets and hidden knowledge. As an NPC, the Knowing Mentor is played by Matthew Mercer and Brennan Lee Mulligan.
is a dwarven Blood cleric of the Raven Queen. She served as the head of the Claret Orders in Tal'Dorei, and remained a member.

This deity was the God of Death preceding the Raven Queen, and one of the deities who founded the world of Exandria. The Raven Queen sundered the name of her predecessor from reality, and as of 812 PD, the first God of Death was largely forgotten. As a PC he was briefly played by Laura Bailey in the prologue of Downfall.

Terrosh, the Lidless Slumber is a one-eyed fey creature that guards a portal between the Taloned Highlands of Exandria, and the edge of the Sablecast Grounds of the Fey Realm. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
__notoc__ is a glaistig fortune teller living in Dol-Makjar. As an NPC, she is played by Brennan Lee Mulligan.
Trush is a shadow demon and patron of the goblin warlock Bol'bara.

was an archmage and malconvoker during the Age of Arcanum who freed the Betrayer Gods from their prisons and became the left hand of Asmodeus. As an NPC in Exandria Unlimited: Calamity, Vespin was played by Brennan Lee Mulligan; the version of him conjured by the Matron of Ravens was played by Matthew Mercer.
Vrylaska Fellbranch was a vampire who murdered Warmaster Mikael Daxio.
is a demigod of the storm. Woden is a former member of the Council of Seven Scepters, where they represented the storm giants.
was an elven wizard and a member of The Wing. He appeared in Vox Machina Origins #2.
Vordo, the Fateshaper, or The Golden Weaver, was the god of fate and order and one of the deities that founded the world of Exandria.
Verna the Viper is a lagomore specialist in esoteric explosives. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.
Headmaster Zivan Margolin is the human Archmage of Conscription in the Cerberus Assembly and the Headmaster of the Soltryce Academy in Rexxentrum.

{{Disambig | Image = Yao Fei (Prime Earth) 0001.jpg | MainPage = Yao Fei (Prime Earth) | AltID = | ImageText = Yao Fei | Era1 = Modern | Description = The Accomplished Perfect Physician is a Chinese super-functionary who can channel powers through his voice. He also has an analytical mind and is a skilled diplomat and investigator. Though he fights for the Tibetan cause, he was a member of the state sponsored Great Ten and its successor, the Great Twenty. Nonetheless, he has rivalries with his teammates August General in Iron and Socialist Red Guardsman over their views on Tibet and politics, respectively. The Accomplished Perfect Physician was created by Grant Morrison and J.G. Jones, first

{{Disambig | Image = Lance Gallant Quality Universe 0001.png | MainPage = Lance Gallant (Quality Universe) | AltID = | ImageText = Lance Gallant | Description = Captain Triumph is a Golden Age superhero who was active during World War II. His twin brother Michael was killed by an act of sabotage, but the Fates kept him on Earth as a ghost. Lance gains superpowers and becomes Captain Triumph by merging with Michael's ghost. This is activated by Lance touching his T-shaped birthmark. Michael is able to operate separately when they are not together. They also became members of the All-Star Squadron. Captain Triumph was created by Alfred Andriola, first appearing in the Quality Comics publicatio

{{Disambig | Image = Chunk_001.jpg | MainPage = Chester Runk (New Earth) | AltID = | ImageText = Chester Runk | Era1 = Iron Age | Description = Chester Runk, known by the nickname Chunk, is a scientist and ally to The Flash. He is also a close personal friend of Wally West. Runk grew up to become overweight, which increased as an adult when he accidentally opened a black hole inside his body. This makes him need to eat vast quantities every day to appease it. Chunk had a son, also named Chester Runk. He lived in Central City, befriended Wally's cousin Ace West, and was also nicknamed Chunk. Chunk was created by Mike Baron and Jackson Guice, first appearing in (1988). Chester Runk II was crea

Cyborg is a young superhero with cybernetic enhancements from his brilliant scientist father. After a terrible lab accident, Victor Stone was fatally injured, only being kept alive by robotic implants made by his father. Cyborg often struggles with his humanity, never being sure if he is more man or machine. He has been an important member of the Teen Titans and the Justice League, making great friends in each who he trusted to appreciate him for who he is. The public also loves him, being a major black superhero and a role model to many.

{{Disambig | Image = The Flash Vol 1 765 Textless.jpg | MainPage = Albert Desmond (Prime Earth) | ImageText = Albert Desmond | Era1 = New 52 | AltID = Albert Desmond | Description = Doctor Alchemy, also known as Mister Element, is a super-villain named Albert Desmond who fights the Flash using the Philosopher's Stone, a mystic object that can transmute elements. He is a member of the Rogues, a loose organization of criminals who fight against the Flash Family, and has also been a member of the Injustice Gang. His identical doppelganger and clone is Alvin Desmond. Doctor Alchemy was created by John Broome and Carmine Infantino, first appearing in (1958). | Gallery = File:Doctor Alchemy 004.jp

{{Disambig | Image = Leonard Fiasco Prime Earth 0001.jpg | MainPage = Leonard Fiasco (Prime Earth) | ImageText = Leonard Fiasco | Era1 = Rebirth | Description = The Eraser is Leonard "Lenny" Fiasco, an enemy of Batman who turned to crime after living his college days under constant mocking and taunting by his classmates. Becoming a professional criminal for hire, he developed a helmet in the shape of a pencil eraser that can eliminate evidence from a crime scene. For a twenty percent commission, before taxes, the Eraser offers his services to any criminal who needs it, removing all their tracks before any police investigation could even be conducted. His brilliant methods make it extremely d

{{Disambig | Image = | MainPage = Rebecca Sharpe (New Earth) | AltID = | ImageText = Becky Sharpe | Description = Hazard is Becky Sharpe, a super-villain and enemy to Infinity, Inc.. Her grandfather was the Gambler, an enemy to Green Lantern and the Justice Society. Her powers allow her to manipulate probability and her motif focuses on gambling. She has also been a member of Injustice Unlimited. Hazard was created by Roy Thomas, Dann Thomas and Todd McFarlane, first appearing in . (1987) | Gallery = File:Rebecca Sharpe Prime Earth 0002.jpg| File:Black Ops.png| File:Mister Hazard 01.png| File:Champ Hazard 1.jpg| File:Roger Sharpe Earth 2 001.jpg| File:Hazard Wildstorm 01.jpg|

{{Disambig | Image = Lyle Bolton PE 01.jpg | MainPage = Lyle Bolton (Prime Earth) | Era1 = New 52 | ImageText = Lyle Bolton | Description = Lock-Up is a law enforcement-obsessed super-villain and an antagonist to Batman. His specialty is developing imprisonment and incarceration systems. During No Man's Land, he was deputized by Batman to hold captured villains in Blackgate Penitentiary. He has been a member of the Secret Society of Super-Villains. Lock-Up was created by Paul Dini, originally appearing in the Batman: The Animated Series episode "Lock-Up" (1994). His first published appearance in the mainstream DC Universe was written by Chuck Dixon in (1996). | Gallery = LockUp 3.jpg| LockUp

Mister Freeze was a renowned scientist whose beloved wife, Nora was diagnosed with a rare illness that would cause her death. As no cure was developed for such illness, Fries used cryogenic technology to freeze Nora's body and preserve it until he found a cure. However, due to a disastrous accident, Freeze was exposed to a series of chemicals that caused his body's homeostasis to change drastically. Freeze's new condition required him to stay at temperatures below zero, turning his skin white. The accident twisted his mind and he began a criminal career to support his mad experiments and his new way of life. His genius intellect allowed him to build a special suit and weapons designed to tur

{{Disambig | Image = Multiplex PE 02.jpg | MainPage = Danton Black (Prime Earth) | ImageText = Danton Black | Era2 = New 52 | AltID = | Description = Multiplex is Danton Black, a metahuman supervillain with the ability to create duplicate bodies of himself. It is unknown how many clones he can generate. His career started as a scientist working with Martin Stein, and he gained powers in the same explosion that created Firestorm. Unlike Firestorm, he decided to use these powers for crime. He has been a member of the Secret Society of Super-Villains and the Suicide Squad. In the New 52 reboot, Multiplex is introduced as a member of the new Secret Society of Super-Villains. Multiplex was create

{{Disambig | Image = Truth & Justice Vol 1 3 Textless Variant.jpg | ImageText = Linton Midnite | MainPage = Linton Midnite (Prime Earth) | Era1 = New 52 | Description = Papa Midnite is a powerful Jamaican voodoo magician. Operating out of New York City using his dead sister's skull as a totem for his magic, Papa Midnite has found himself to be a rival and even an enemy to John Constantine. In the New 52 reboot, Papa Midnite's nationality is changed to be Haitian, but his rivalry with Constantine remains the same. Papa Midnite was created by Jamie Delano and John Ridgway, first appearing in (1988). | Gallery = File:Papa Midnite.JPG|

{{Disambig | Image = Roger Hayden (Prime Earth) 0010.jpeg | ImageText = Roger Hayden | MainPage = Roger Hayden (Prime Earth) | Era1 = The New 52 | Description = The Psycho-Pirate is a legacy of super-villains with psychological themes. *The original was Charles Halstead, an enemy of the Justice Society who committed crimes based on different emotions. *His successor was Roger Hayden, who wears a Medusa Mask that can manipulate the emotions of others. This mask has arguably driven him insane over the years. Hayden was a member of the Secret Society of Super-Villains until Black Adam killed him during Infinite Crisis. *He once switched places with James Highwater to escape the insanity brought

Ra's al Ghul is an international eco-terrorist that commands an incredibly large army of trained people under the name of League of Assassins. Ra's has managed to overcome death and has lived longer than any human thanks to the use of a mysterious natural phenomenon known as Lazarus Pit, which restores the youth and health of any person that uses it at the expense of temporary insanity. Due to his long lifespan, Ra's has adopted the philosophy of eliminating the majority of the human kind for the greater good of the planet. His destructive plans were always disrupted by Batman, the only person capable to match Ra's own intellect and skills. Because of this, Ra's tried to made Batman the righ

{{Disambig | Align = | Image = | MainPage = Walter Shreeve (DCAU) | AltID = | Era1 = DCAU | ImageText = Walter Shreeve | Description = Shriek was a scientist named Walter Shreeve who worked at Wayne-Powers. Eventually, he was contracted by the CEO Derek Powers to kill Bruce Wayne and the new Batman; Terry McGinnis, using his sonic supersuit. After losing his hearing in a confrontation with McGinnis, Shreeve vowed revenge against him. Shriek was created by Stan Berkowitz, first appearing in the Batman Beyond episode, "Shriek" (1999). | Gallery = File:Augusto Gutierrez 001.jpg|

{{Disambig | Align = | Image = Monster 03.jpg | MainPage = Stanley Dover II (New Earth) | AltID = | Era1 = Iron Age | ImageText = Stanley Dover | Description = Stanley Dover was a young kid from Star City who had adventures with his monster Spot, the demon also known as "the Beast With No Name". Stanley's grandfather, Stanley Dover Sr. was an amateur occultist known as the Star City Slayer who hunted and murdered young children to use their blood as a means to attract the Beast. He crossed paths with Green Arrow, whose body he had hoped to take over in order to further his cause. Eventually, the man was killed by the demonic beast in revenge for the torture he had inflicted on his grandson S

{{Disambig | Image = Sharon_Vance_Prime Earth_001.jpg | ImageText = Sharon Vance | MainPage = Sharon Vance (Prime Earth) | Era1 = Rebirth | Description = Strange Visitor, real name Sharon Vance, is a being of pure energy. She was originally from Smallville, but gained her powers when a lightning strike merged her with the cosmic being Kismet. She has a loose association to the Superman Family. Sharon Vance was created by Randall Frenz, Ron Frenz and Sal Buscema, making her first appearance in (1999). | Gallery = File:Strange_Visitor_01.jpg| File:Kismet 004.jpg| File:Kismet Prime Earth 0001.png|

{{Disambig | Align = | Image = | MainPage = Kal-El (New Earth) | AltID = | Era1 = Modern | ImageText = Kal-El | Description = Superman Red is an alternate version of Superman created when the hero used a mind enhancing machine powered by Kryptonite to increase his intelligence. The radiation caused Superman to split into two super-intelligent beings; the Superman Blue and Superman Red. Eventually, they saved the world together and married Lana Lang and Lois Lane respectively. In the New Earth, Superman used a Red and Blue containment suit when he experienced a weird power fluctuation that rendered him in the form of pure energy. He found that he was considerably faster, intangible, and able

The Swamp Thing is an elemental creature birthed from a mass of vegetable matter that absorbed the memories and personality of botanist Alec Holland. He lives in the swamp of Louisiana, and is the guardian of the Green, the energy network that connects Earth's plant life, and has found himself an ally of Earth's heroes, such as the Justice League, John Constantine, and the Batman. As one of DC's most celebrated and recognized horror characters, there's a lot of content to sift through with the Swamp Thing, and this guide should be able to help readers interested in reading about his adventures.

{{DC Database:Character Template | Image = Vicki Grant.png | RealName = Victoria Grant | MainAlias = Vicki Grant | Aliases = Futura; Sunspot; Ice; Grasshopper; Twilight, Mistress of the Dark; Windsong; Molecular Maiden; Hypno Girl; Midnight Wisp; Strato-Girl, Mistress of the Wind; Goldgirl; Alchemiss; Dimension Girl; Stellar; Ultra Girl; Starlet; Cardinal; Aniwoman; Thumbelina; Tiarra Star; Matter Girl; Echo; Ariel; Black; Weather Witch; Emerald Tiger; Rainbeaux, Mistress of Color; Hummingbird; Hydra, Goddess of the Sea; Hyptella; Sonik; Puma, the She-Cat; Sulphur; Sparrow Hawk; Kismet, Mistress of the Mind Wave; Plant Mistress; Sea`Mist; Harp; Pixie; Snowfall; Glass Lass; Unicorn; Queen of

{{Disambig | Image = Guy Gardner Prime Earth 014.jpeg | MainPage = Guy Gardner (Prime Earth) | ImageText = Guy Gardner | Era1 = Modern Age | Description = Warrior is an alias used by the hero Guy Gardner. Gardner began using the name after he lost his status as a Green Lantern. Originally he wore his Yellow Lantern Ring and an exo-skeleton, but these were destroyed by Parallax. When he discovered his Vuldarian heritage, he used the name to continue their war against the Tormocks. This revelation in physiology allowed him to transform his body into various weapons. Later on, Guy would open up his own bar called Warriors. The Warrior alias was created by Chuck Dixon and Mitch Byrd, first appea
Devi Cassl is an Awoken Paladin and one of the two that commands the Royal Army
Grayris, Baroness is a Taken Captain located at the Shattered Coast when a Taken corruption event occurs.
Gahlran, the Sorrow-Bearer was a Cabal who was controlled by the Crown of Sorrow.
Ir Anûk, Deathsinger is a Hive Wizard ultra in the Destiny: The Taken King raid King's Fall. She was the twin sister of Ir Halak and the daughter of Oryx, the Taken King.
Inotam, Oblivion's Triune was a Psion Flayer that formed from a joining ritual derived from ancient texts of the mind.

The Imminent Mind is a member of the Sol Progeny that guards the Black Heart in the Black Garden. It is similar to the Eschaton Mind, but has a large ring on its head, similar to the Descendants. It wields a Torch Hammer. It represents the present. It is the Axis Mind of the Vex programming Sol Imminent.
Kargen, the Technocrat was a Psion Flayer. He is the boss of Insight Terminus strike.
Kandorak is a Hive Knight ultra. He appears in the story mission The First Firewall.
Ozletc, the Sky Piercer was a Psion Flayer that served in the Red Legion. She represented Arc energy within the Psion Flayers.
Niruul, the Hollow Voice was a Psion Flayer that served in the Red Legion. She represented Void energy within the Psion Flayers.
Pujari was a Warlock who had a vision where he entered the Black Garden.
Tinasha-3 was an Iron Lord who was also known as Ashraven. She was a Warlock. She took part in the Iron Lord's battle against SIVA.

The Vex are ancient metal warriors, linked together and governed by Axis Minds. Unlike most species, they don't understand hostility, as the species had a common threat on their planet. As a result, what the beings found in the Solar System perceive as hostility is in reality simply the vex attempting to convert everything into something that makes sense to them.
An Salaak, the Weft is a Taken Wizard found in an Ascendant Challenge with An Hamaat, the Warp, and has the capability to control the movement or placement of Blight.
Agraenth, Proxy was a Cabal Legionary simulation seen in the Infinite Forest, paired with Caourg, Proxy and Guurn, Proxy, acting as a Daemon firewall to intercept any intruder(s).

Amira was a member of the Black Armory. During the Collapse, she tried to flee with the rest of the Black Armory to a nearby bunker, and as Henriette Meyrin watched, she was engulfed by a cloud of a poisonous gas that withered her down to the bone.

The Apprentice of the Cryptoglyph are special Hive Wizards seen in the In the Deep Mission, where they are responsible for maintaining and guarding the Cryptoglyph within the Catacombs of the Moon. They, along with their masters, would ambush The Guardian who pursued their key artifact with the intent of keeping it from falling into their hands.
Barrier Hobgoblins are elite Hobgoblin units belonging to the Vex, enhanced with barrier ablities.

The Consul was an aristocratic member of the Cabal Praetorate and the mentor and personal advisor of Dominus Ghaul, as well as the mastermind behind the Midnight Coup that overthrew Emperor Calus. He was the secondary antagonist of Destiny 2.

Cragur, Plague of the Well is a massive Hive Ogre who is encountered as a Tier 4 boss in the Blind Well, when the curse of the Dreaming City is on its second week. It was created for the purpose of consuming the light of the Well.
The Devourer of Tainted Light is a Cabal War Beast that devoured Dark Ether from Screebs, causing it to become aggressive and brutally murder Shadow Legion troops.
Dendrite, Studious Mind is a ranking Hydra Vex Mind in charge of coordinating Sol Collective operations within Creation. It serves as the final boss of the Solo Ops activity, Creation.

Decima, Shielding Psion is an Imperial Cabal Psion sent by Empress Caiatl alongside Thysaeuc, Quicksilver Psion and Nuajes, Hacking Psion to assist the Guardian in breaching Bunker WAR-6 to stop Maya Sundaresh from using a Warsat to expand the influence of her Echo of Command.

The Drenched Sorceress was a Hive Wizard in charge of Hive Rituals in the Sinking Docks. Her activities were quickly noticed by the Vanguard and an Assassination order would be put on her. Despite being flanked by Arc-shielded Revenant Knights, she met her demise by the hand of The Guardian.
The Empathic Minotaur is a Major Vex Minotaur seen in the My Captain Adventure, where it is seen in the Vex trial during the search for Captain Masoud Jacobson‏.
Ei Räkosh, Banisher of Memory is a Hive Lightbearer Wizard encountered within The Forgotten Deep Lost Sector in The Pale Heart.

F'shor, Cryptolith Keeper is a Hive Wizard that was corrupted into a Wrathborn serving Xivu Arath, God of War. They appeared in the Creation facility of the Bray Exoscience in the Heist Battleground: Europa activity, and attempted to corrupt the Clovis Bray AI into a Wrathborn alongside its fellow keepers.
Golur the Plagued is a Hive Knight found in the Penumbral Depths, where they attempt to kill the Guardian with a swarm of Thrall.
Haraal, Venom of Oryx is a Taken Wizard appearing as a boss in the Shard of the Traveler Subclass Quest for the Hunter Nightstalker ability.
Guurn, Proxy was a Cabal Legionary simulation seen in the Infinite Forest, paired with Caourg, Proxy and Agraenth, Proxy, acting as a Daemon firewall to intercept any intruder(s).
Hathrek, the Glasweard is a Hive Lightbearer Wizard who appears as the boss of the Extraction Lost Sector in Savathûn's Throne World.

Halsiks is an associate working for the House of Spider crime syndicate and acts as the navigator of Spider's Ketch. He is encountered across Ketchcrash and Expedition activities, assisting the Guardians in fending off against thieving pirates. Halsiks looks much like any Spider's Associate, armored with a suit covered in green quills and wearing a full face helmet. He always uses a Wire Rifle, and he's described as "deadly with it", with characters often remarking on his keen eyes and shooting prowess.

Iliksis, Light Stalker was a powerful Fallen Captain of the House of Devils who launched a full-scale assault on the tower known as Bannerfall, in an attempt to breach the walls of the Last City. However, his efforts were thwarted by the Guardian, who happened to be there searching for blueprints and components to forge a new Gjallarhorn.

Ir Nagash, Second Aria is a Hidden Swarm Deathsinger seen in the Choir of the Damned Mission, where the Wizard along with her coven and leader, Ir Airâm, Deathsinger, would be hunted and killed by The Guardian to gather their essence in hopes of creating the Deathbringer.

Ilhali is a Psion advisor who serves Emperor Calus aboard the Leviathan. They and Tlu'arg helped Calus during his wallowing sadness following his exile by mocking Ghaul's brutality. They would later be tasked by Calus to ready his automatons after hearing the news of Ghaul's death.
Ir Akraht, Light Harvester is a Major Hive Wizard of the Lucent Brood encountered in the Cosmodrome, tasked with purifying the Light stolen from the Guardians.

Interrogator Orm is a Psion of the Barant Imperium encountered during the Fearsome Retainer Mission. They have no special mechanics, but defeating Orm and their troops is required to progress the mission.

Kargen, the Technocrat is a high-ranking Psion Flayer and one of the Red Legion's foremost experts on Vex technology. He and his team pillaged countless Vex sites and later attempted to hack the Insight Terminus on Nessus.

Iraz, Eye of Savathûn is a Taken Wizard that served as the final boss in the mission, Unexpected Guests. Sent by Savathûn to Io, possibly as a proxy for the spread of Blight, their presence there was of great concern for Ikora Rey. They would be summoned and slain by The Guardian.

Ithyks, the Scrapworker was a Fallen Marauder and a master in the art of scrapworking. She was hired by Eramis, the Shipstealer, to hunt for the relics of Nezarec on behalf of the Witness. She was encountered in the Pirate Hideout: The Scrapworker activity.
Ixis is a House of Salvation Apothecary from Riis. She was captured by the Revenant Scorn, but working with Eido, created a tonic that could destroy the Revenant leader, Fikrul.

Irkaril of Xivu Arath is a Hive Wizard of Xivu Arath's Horde leading a ritual coven attempting to open a path into Ascendant Plane in the Hull Breach. They serve as one of the bosses of the Nether activity.

Kridis, Dark Priestess is a Fallen Baroness from the House of Salvation and the Archon of its Prime Servitor, Yamiks Prime. She is a close friend of Eramis, Kell of Darkness and a member of her inner council who will stop at nothing to advance Eramis's cause. Following her departure from the House of Devils, Kridis devoted herself to the study of the Darkness and became a skilled practitioner of Stasis. Later, she assumed leadership of House Salvation and attempted to rebuild her House and awake Eramis from her slumber.

Lii'liks, Harvester of the Witness is a large Scorn Abomination, engorged off of Dark Ether, and the main antagonist of the Wild Card mission. It would lead efforts to corrupt the Pale Heart and its inhabitants by engorging Screebs with Tainted Dark Ether.
The Lord of Every Nothing, also known as the will-without-will, is an enigmatic force and master of the Dire Taken.

Mav is a Guardian who attempted to steal an unknown item on the Moon but was ambushed by the Taken. She created a Ward of Dawn while her companion wearing Celestial Nighthawk fired their Golden Gun at the Taken Ogre.
Melissos, Swarm Mind is a Wyvern Vex Mind of the Nessian Schism and is one of the four secret Strangelet Capsule world bosses encountered in The Edge of Fate's mythic difficulty campaign.

The Nightmare of Zydron, Gate Lord is the Nightmare of the Vex Gate Lord and protector of the Endless Steps on Venus: Zydron. Recreated with the power of the Darkness by the Lunar Pyramid, it serves as the Aspect of Servitude.
Nolthok, the Withering is a Taken Wizard encountered during The Sunless Cell Strike.

Ozletc, the Sky Piercer was a Psion Flayer serving the Red Legion seen hidden in Mercury's future. A co-leader along with her sisters Niruul and Tazaroc, she represented Arc energy and was the eldest of her family. She served as the second boss among the rotating bosses of The Sundial.
Overload Chieftains are powerful Champions of the Scorn, enhanced with powers of the Darkness.

Optus Ulios, Coalition Ally is a Cabal Psion and an Optus of the Imperial Cabal. They twice accompanied Empress Caiatl to the Underbelly of the Derelict Leviathan when she went in there to challenge the Nightmare of Dominus Ghaul.

Pritk, Deathsinger Trio is a Hive Wizard and Deathsinger of Xivu Arath's Horde striving to challenge the Guardian's claim to the Taken Throne. They are accompanied by their fellow Deathsingers Tuis and Soume. They serve as one of the bosses of the Court of Blades activity.
A Redolence of Decay is a Darkness-empowered Shadow Legion soldier that appears aboard Essence during the Root of Nightmares Raid.

Raneiks Unified is an amalgamation of ten Servitors horrifically fused together through unknown circumstances and serves as one of the hosts of the Corrupted Puppeteer. It is encountered in the Castor Complex aboard the Vesper Station, serving as the first boss of the Vesper's Host Dungeon.
Räkta, the Mournful is a Major Hive Wizard that can be seen guarding the Mesh Layers in the Refinery during the Hive version of the Sepiks Perfected Strike.
Rhaska, Subjugator of Thresholds is a Harbinger of the Witness who led Taken and Dread forces within The Impasse in an attempt to take control of it.

Sekrion, Nexus Mind was a massive Vex Hydra that lives deep within Venus. It is the Vex Mind in charge of converting Venus into a Machine World and served as the final boss of "The Nexus" Strike. In The Dawning, Sekrion would return as Sekrion, Subverted Mind.

Sulhava, Vassal to Xol is a Hive Wizard who is encountered in Alton Dynamo during Will of the Thousands. Sulhava leads the Hive in one of the rooms which the Guardians must clear before facing Xol, Will of the Thousands.
Stichos, the Dampening Mind is one of three powerful Vex Minotaurs maintaining the dampening field to prevent the Kepler singularity from growing.
The Forgotten is a powerful Nightmare Chieftain found on the Derelict Leviathan.

The Corrupted Puppeteer is an AI built by the Clovis Bray corporation using Vex technology, which Clovis Bray I intended as a programmable Vex Mind for observing their kind. It was originally confined aboard Vesper Station, until debris from the Morning Star impacted the station and set it loose, enabling it to transfer itself into a Fallen Exo body. When Fallen refugees from the House of Salvation attempted to establish a community near the station and build an Ether refinery, it began to hunt them down and assimilated their minds into its collective consciousness. With the Fallen under its command, it continued to coordinate the construction of the Anomaly next to the Station as a communic

The Ferrule, Subjugator of Locks is a Subjugator and member of the party led by Kerrev, the Erased that infiltrated Rhulk's Pyramid in search of something deep within they believed could help change them into new forms. Prior to joining Kerrev on the journey, they had been silent, only stating that they would be themselves when thinking of what they could be through the journey.
The Strider, also known by her real name Mikaela Julaha, was the first Cloud Strider to defend Neomuna.

Umra, Xol Spawn was a Major Hive Wizard who was encountered in The Abomination Heist Strike. She tried to prevent the Guardians from unlocking the door in the Gatehouse, but she ultimately fell in battle.

Ugul Gar Knights are a class of Hive Knights within the Grasp of Nokris. Brought back from death by Nokris's powers of necromancy, they give off a green glow and carry Hive Relics that can be used to destroy crystals of condensed Soulfire.

Tuis, Deathsinger Trio is a Hive Wizard and Deathsinger of Xivu Arath's Horde striving to challenge the Guardian's claim to the Taken Throne. They are accompanied by their fellow Deathsingers Pritk and Soume. They serve as one of the bosses of the Court of Blades activity.
Tristak was a member of the House of Salvation who was transformed into a Revenant Scorn during the Revenant Uprising.
The Totality Psion is the common Minor variant of the Psion in the Totality Division.

Valus Trau'ug is a Cabal Centurion found in the Prison of Elders and commander of a renegade group called the Broken Legion. Trau'ug had requested permission from the Cabal high command to attack the Reef but was denied. Impatient with their perceived weakness, he and his soldiers murdered his officers and went AWOL, attacking the Reef. They were captured all the same. How the Reef Awoken defeated Trau'ug is not known and Variks skirts the issue when pressed but Trau'ug's bloodlust and mastery of wartime stratagem is intact within the Prison. Using his battle-tested Cabal field techniques, the "Broken Legion" crush any who dare accept Trau'ug's challenge. His custom-rigged shield randomizes

Vekron, the Conductive Mind is a powerful Vex Mind that is the boss of the Warlock Stormcaller subclass quest "A Spark in Shadow", acting as a conductor of Arc Energy. Under the supervision of Ikora Rey, the Mind was hunted down and destroyed in order to use its Arc Energy to continue the path of becoming a Stormcaller.
Visages of Xol are Elite class Wizards within the Grasp of Nokris. They are seen conducting a ritual on Mars as a means to obtain support from the forces of Savathûn.

Wyr, the Taken is a Taken Wizard encountered in the Story mission Sacrilege. They are one of the three Wizards, the others being Norr, the Taken and Erruk, the Taken, to attempt to siphon the Traveler's energy on Io along with Irausk, Herald of Savathûn. However they and their coven would be discovered and wiped out by The Guardian.
Xiana McCaig was the water ocean expert of the New Pacific Arcology.

Xillox, Oppression of Xivu Arath was a Hive Wrathborn Wizard serving Xivu Arath, God of War. Sometime following her corruption, the Spider tasked the Guardian to hunt the Wizard and put an end to her misery.

Šimmumah ur-Nokru is a Hive Wizard who is encountered in Penumbral Depths during the Strange Terrain mission. After being summoned by a group of four Knights, Šimmumah had to be defeated to progress. They would later be revived as a Lightbearer, taking the title Lucent Necromancer, and join Savathûn's Lucent Brood. During the events of Season of the Deep, they would attempt a ritual to resurrect Oryx, the Taken King by force through a ritual involving the use of Necromancy and a Hive Ghost.

Yishra is a noble Wizard of the Hidden Swarm and one of two daughters of Voshyr. She is a granddaughter of Crota, Son of Oryx and a key member in the Scarlet Court. Yishra, along with her mother, sister, aunt, and cousin all attended the gathering with the High Celebrant of Xivu Arath. She was subsequently killed along with her sister and mother by a Daybreak thrown by the Warlock Osiris.
Chengat, a grand mage, was one of the first masters of the Yshari Sanctum. He crafted the rings Focus and Restraint to work in conjunction with one another to bolster the user's mental fortitude.

Chakku was the high arcanist of the Taan Mage Clan. He exiled two prodigious trainees for creating a powerful artifact with great potential to be abused. By 1272, one of the exiles returned for the core of the artifact. Chakku was killed when he tried to stop him.

Dark Vessels (Triune Vessels in early concepts) are cultists of the Coven, specifically trained to summon demons and immediately become possessed by them. However, as the resulting mindless construct of flesh and bone is highly unstable, they must start the process in combat, giving enemy time to kill the cultist before the ritual is complete.
Dark Cardinal Maldul is a Stronghold Boss encountered in Altar of Ruin. He is a super unique Dark Summoner.
Cyrik was the student of Zayl. He sought to harness the powers of death in the same way the Nephalem did, but this time, to better serve the Balance.
Ethad was a grand mage who lived around 500 years before the time of the Horadrim. He crafted the Oculus.

The Enslaved Magus is a type of undead monster encountered in Diablo Immortal. In life, the Magi were Horadrim, sent to invade the Library of Zoltun Kulle. However, Kulle defeated them and resurrected them as his undead slaves.
The Fly Host is a monster encountered in Diablo IV. It walks around, birthing flies to attack the player.
Giyua is a figure in Umbaru mythology, said to be the guardian of the Unformed Land. According to the Umbaru, it is Giyua who greets the spirits of those who have departed the mortal realm.

Brother Fyntana was a member of the Monks of Ivgorod. He embarked on a quest to rid Aranoch of the lacuni. After losing his hand, he comissioned a replacement. It is said that bits of the lacuni he killed were incorporated into its construction. Fyntana apparently failed in his quest (in that lacuni can still be found in Aranoch), but his fabled quest was recorded in Poldamyr's Histories of the Veradani.

The Horadric Judicar is a undead monster encountered in the Master's Sanctum zone in the Library of Zoltun Kulle in Diablo Immortal. In life, the Judicar were Horadrim, sent to invade the Library of Zoltun Kulle. However, Kulle defeated them and resurrected them as his undead slaves.

Infectus the Reckoner was a unique Walking Corpse found in the Fallen Den during pre-release development of Diablo III. Infectus had an early version of the Arcane Enchanted monster trait, summoning Arcane Pets that can easily kill lower level players.
Inhora is/was a Crusader to came to the aid of Ivgorod. (S)he was presented with the Omnislash by the Patriarch Seph in gratitude for such deeds.
Iskatu, Minion of Diablo was a Terror Demon in service to the Lord of Terror.
Jostan is/was a Master Necromancer of the Priests of Rathma.

Kara Nightshadow was a Necromancer of the Priests of Rathma. Ebony-skinned and considered attractive by many of her kin, Kara always carried with her the traditional weapon of the priests, the ivory dagger. She disliked the Vizjerei, considering them untrustworthy.
Lakumba was a member of the Umbaru. It is said that of the 'thread' that extends from the Unformed Land into the mortal realm, she was unrivaled in her ability to 'weave' it, revealing hidden truths.

The Khazra Abomination is a mutated khazra, and is the boss of the Forsaken Quarry and Hoarfrost Demise s in Diablo IV. It attacks through melee, though its swings can send out bile, dealing AOE damage in pools. It can also slam the ground, creating a bile pool.

Lethes is a rogue Necromancer. Megolomaniacal, Lethes has little regard for life, and pursues her goals ruthlessly. She has little patience for subtlety. Lethes could have been Deathspeaker if not for her disdain of Balance. Though she proudly advocated for resilient undead nations, her necromancy was often imprecise. After she spread curses through the Necropolis, Lethes was put on trial by her mentor, Xul. She fled, abandoning her dream of a dead kingdom... until she discovered a Worldstone shard.
Maghda was a witch, a minion of Belial, and the ruthless leader of the Coven.

Lord Death (or simply Death) is the supposed personification of death in at least one of Sanctuary's cultures. Supposedly, he is a kindly figure. Legends say that ravens serve as Death's couriers, carrying souls to the afterlife.

Elder Brother Lyam is a member of the Alliance of the Dying Sun. During or prior to the End of Days, he placed a number of portals that led to Set Dungeons. In Khanduras, he placed a portal inside Leoric's crypt. He was disappointed that he did not encounter the Mad King himself, being so close to his lair. Lyam placed further portals in the High Heavens and Pandemonium Fortress. He wrote to the Alliance on his achievements, noting his hope that they would never doubt his abilities again.

Mykan was a deathspeaker of the Priests of Rathma during the early days of the order. A gifted individual known for his sharp wits and even sharper tongue, he wrote many of the order's strongest spells.
Nathrum was a Doomwarden who resided in the Halls of Damnation, in charge with extracting Light from captive angels. He was slain by a hero/group of heroes in service to the angel Zepydra.
Oblivion Knights (a.k.a. Undead Horrors) are undead soldiers used by the Burning Hells.

:"As Malthael has imbued them with the ability to sense the living, revenant archers do not rely on their vision to find their targets. There is no place safe from their sightless gaze. They will find you through stone, wood, and even the ground itself. And once they have their quarry, they do not miss."—Lorath Nahr Revenant Archers are a type of undead Reaper.

Rethald was a summoner of demons, and claimed he could control any such hellspawn he called. A demon ended up consuming him. Afterwards, the demon has been killed, and its skull was made into a helmet.
Razeth was an individual with necromatic powers. If one did not fear him, they feared the dark power of his minions.
The Soul Killer Shaman is the Fetish Shaman is the Fetish Shaman who led the fetishes that attacked Port Justinian in 1270. He was killed by the Shard-seeker.

Szab was a Necromancer. He was the first outsider to meet the Umbaru. He tried to explain the philosophy of the Priests of Rathma to them, but the language barrier proved to be too great. Thus, instead of giving his philisophical beliefs, he told them of Trag'Oul, and that he lived among the stars.

Tendaji was an Umbaru. At some point, (s)he followed the whispers of spirits into the jungle, hoping to hoping to learn their secrets. Here, Tendaji found a staff called the Diviner. The voice of SuWong came to the staf's new owner, echoing clearly as long as Tendaji held the weapon. he showed Tendaji the ways of the Unformed Land, which became Tendaji's ways as well.

The Arch-Litch Malignus is an cut boss enemy. He was supposed to appear in Level 16 just like Sir Gorash. He's an Undead version of Hell Mages, though he's set to Demon type, and would work like their last variant - Advocate. He has his own sounds which are a bit modified Hell Mages sounds. He doesn't work in the game as there seems to be a problem with his graphics. File:Arch-Litch Malignus Attack.gif|Malignus Attack File:Arch-Litch Malignus Special.gif|Malignus Teleport File:Arch-Litch Malignus Death.gif|Malignus Death
Terror Zealots are members of the Cult of Terror. They often reach a point of devotion where they produce congealed terror from their tear glands.
The Wandering Priest was an individual who hailed from the Low Hills. They created the Holy Point Shot during an ecstatic trance.

The Walkers are dark agents of the underworld. Their origin is a mystery, and the few that dare speak of them believe the Walkers to be emissaries of Hell itself. Some claim the Walkers are demons, but this is hearsay. Nevertheless, folks swear that a Walker's wake carries the scent of rotting eggs.

Zaboul, Lord of Wrath is/was a demon who was active prior to the Dark Exile. When the Prime Evils declared that they would not invade Sanctuary, he forged the Burst of Wrath. A thousand demons died in the process.
Wughan was a master of the Monks of Ivgorod. He was the first to master the six techniques the Monks use, and weaved them into his own fighting style.

The Eater Bit is a digital lifeform. Erika Mishima created them after hacking an Eater (Purebreed Mode) to help her with her hacking. After losing consciousness however, they attack her and merge with her to create Eater Legion Attacks *Spread Shot: The smaller Eater Bits gather round the biggest one in a circle, then fire Beams from their eyes. *Assault Rush: All Eater Bits charge, ramming into the enemy one by one.

Gengomon is a Translation Appmon. A skilled translator who knows all the languages of the world, it has the ability to disrupt conversations by forcibly translating what the other person is saying. Attacks * *
Giant Slayer is a Robot. Attacks *Finger Bomb *Holy Flare *Purifying Light

Jishomon is a Dictionary Appmon. An Appmon that looks like a thick dictionary. It hates information on the internet that originates from unknown sources, and always believes only in the knowledge it possesses. Attacks *Biblio-Scan *Secret Glyph (Hidden Glyph)

Kaimon is a Shopping Appmon. An Appmon that will always sell the items in the basket at a bargain price. Once it has caught a customer's eye, it will never let them go until they buy the item. Attacks *Price Bargain (Bargain Price) *Bulk Buy (Bakugai Time)

Kosomon is a Gossip Review Appmon. A slightly suspicious Appmon who is always sneaking around with someone. It calls itself an "informed insider," and will tell you secret information if you talk to it. Attacks *Chatter Paper (Idobata Paper) *Stealth Work (Kossori Work)

Libramon is a Library Appmon. It is the caretaker of a huge library and a collector of rare books. It has the ability to turn any Appmon that catches its eye into text data and turn it into a book. Attacks *Verbal Jail *Devil's Codex

Luckmon is a Slot Appmon. A slot machine-type Appmon that will spit out coins when three pictures line up. There is always a line of Appmon in front of it, hoping to get rich quick. Attacks *Lucky Slot *Triple Seven
NeoMyotismon Darkness Mode Two is the DigiFuse of NeoMyotismon Darkness Mode One and MetalGreymon (2010 anime).

Rene is a Digimon. Learning by observing Hinukamuy, Jesmon acquired At, Rene, and Pol as part of its ascetic training. They are able to move and act independently under Jesmon's instructions, and boast formidable behavioral abilities such as direct attacks on the enemy, protection of Jesmon, and rescue of other Digimon.

Reviewmon is a Review Appmon. It is a harsh reviewer who assesses and evaluates everything. It is said that any product or store that it praises becomes very popular. Attacks *Bold Review (Post Review) *

Supplemon is a Supplement Appmon. An Appmon that prescribes highly effective preventative medicine. It is said that if you take the supplements given by Supplemon, you won't catch a cold during that season. Attacks *Vital Supplement (Vital Supple) *Rising Energy (Minagiru Energy)

Tumblemon is a Rock Digimon. It is an In-Training Digimon that grows by eating rocks. Because its digestive system is not fully developed yet, it stores an amount of ore in its body unimaginable given its small size, and gradually converts it into nourishment. The site in which its eye is located also serves as its mouth, and it seems to turn completely blind while eating. Attacks *Rock Breath: Spits out rocks from its large mouth.

Kazuki Suzune is a character in Digimon Liberator (Web Novel). =Profile= A 25-year-old housewife married to the lead developer at T.A.L.E. who created the metaverse pod used in operating Digimon Liberator. A longtime fan of anime and games, she has dipped her toes into Digimon previously due to her brother's influence. She had a privileged upbringing yet is thrifty and pragmatic. Aware of her husband's financial uncertainty, she takes up an investigative role on the debugging team, considering it her part-time job. During the beta test, she encountered a wild Yukidarumon and convinced it to become her partner. =Deck= Suzune uses a Ice-Snow Control deck that includes the following cards: =Car

Rindo Izumo is the lead protagonist of Digimon Eggs. =Profile= Rindo Izumo, becomes entangled in a great destiny after a mysterious encounter with a Digimon. Furthermore, Izumo's right arm seems to possess some kind of special power. =Appearances=

Soda Raito was one of the main antagonists of the Tactics Arc in Digimon Beatbreak prior to his reformation. He's a Cleaner and a former member of Tactics under his self-proclaimed leadership of Team 7. =Profile= Member of Tactics Team Seven. A naturally gifted genius who can do anything after seeing it just once. Likes: boardgames, collecting bandanas. Dislikes: natto.

*Ibrahim Vaughn Holtzman enters orbit and using immediate communication, he reveals the Holtzman Waves to six systems moving them against his father. *Wars of Reunification, consequent of the immediate communication begin. *After an attempt to destroy him, he loses control.

After the liberation of Ix Omnius attempted to recapture the planet in 123 BG. Quentin Butler was there and defended the planet although he regretted to have lost so many fighters and civilians. During the attempt he fought combat robots in the deepest cave channels with 7 of his companions until an explosion caused a cave-in; he was buried alive, until clawed and pushed, finally working his way upward to the amazed shouts of other jihadis who had never expected to find him alive. That battle fixed him as a hero and earned him many accolades.

Ammon was the Mentat of House Ordos during the early First Spice War. He was in charge of the Ordos operations on Arrakis. Ammon was executed on the alleged charge of embezzlement and replaced by Edric O.

(right) from the cover of Dune: The Machine Crusade.]] A Cymek was an advanced form of thinking machine which was once living human, but at some point in time had been converted into a cyborg: a robotic body controlled by a legacy human brain. They lived in the ten-or-so millennia before the establishment of the Spacing Guild. The cymek's human brain was held in a preservation canister filled with electrafluid. In this state, and with frequent upkeep, the brain could live for tens of thousands of years, and could control interchangeable robotic bodies through thoughtrodes.

A Contaminator was a hideously-deformed mutant spawned from the Tleilaxu Flesh Vats. They appear as an infantry unit in Emperor: Battle for Dune, where it is available to any factions affiliated with the Bene Tleilax sub-faction of It carries a lethal virus, capable of turning human beings into additional Contaminators. Any infantry killed in close combat with a Contaminator will be reborn as a Contaminator, under the command of the player controlling the original Contaminator. The Contaminator is only effective against infantry, however; its attack is extremely weak against enemy vehicles and structures.

Guilt-casters were a specialized type of Bene Gesserit member of the Sisterhood who would bombard their ordered and intended victims with waves and pulses of psychic energy, while telling them of great guilt or disappointment they had caused the organization. The most infamous guilt-caster employed by the Sisterhood was one named Stokia, who was used by the women to disable and render harmless Tessia Vernius of Ix. Other intended victims of guilt-casting were Lady and Duchess Jessica Atreides, when she visited Wallach IX; and Lady Margot Fenring exiled on Salusa Secundus. With Duchess Jessica, the Lady herself was able to beat off Stokia's attacks, with advice given by Tessia herself. Margot

{Eencyclopedia}} Karmara al-Jofar was a Fremen and arguably the most prominent wind-etching artist during the Atreidean period. He etched the architraves in the great meeting hall of Paul Muad'Dib's palace at Arrakeen. Some said that even his best work did not match that of the Master of Rifana Sietch, an unknown desert Fremen of the 9800s whose work is not known to survive.

The Kwisatz Mother was a Reverend Mother responsible for the entire Kwisatz Haderach breeding program during a period of time. She had access to the entirety of Other Memory to help guide her in the direction of the program.
Mentat Marko was the Mentat of House Harkonnen. They taught and guided another Mentat, Radnor, who ultimately assassinated them and took their place as Baron Harkonnen's primary Mentat.

The Mother Commander is the leader of the New Sisterhood, which is a blending of the Honored Matres and the Bene Gesserit. Headquartered on Chapterhouse, the Mother Commander was responsible for the training of the New Sisterhood, and for preparing a defense against the Outside Enemy. The first Mother Commander was Murbella.

Amilene Santor d'Sivis is a wizard under the employ of the Twelve. She resides in the Citadel of the Twelve within the Silverwall ward of Stormreach, on the continent of Xen'drik. She lives in the Citadel of the Twelve, though she spends most of her time in the nearby House Kundarak enclave, where the dwarves have given her her own private office. She holds the title "First Stonespeaker," and is the most adept House Sivis user of speaking stones in Stormreach. In general, she remains neutral to the politics of the city, and is well liked by most.

Ak'ash'eck was a sahuagin druid who roamed the northern fringe of the Shargon's Teeth some years ago. He developed his own magic item, a water whip, which he used to prey on ships sailing from Khorvaire to Xen'drik. He gained some infamy by using the water whip to ensnare passengers aboard their vessels and pulling them underwater before anyone even noticed they were missing.
Bel Shalor, called the Shadow in the Flame, is an Overlord of corruption and shadows.
The Blood Queen is an ancient elf vampire cleric of the Qabalrin, a now-extinct elven civilization that occupied the Ring of Storms in Xen'drik, who now fights for the Umbragen.
A blob of annihilation is a titanic and all-consuming ooze said to be formed when cosmic entropy coagulates around the remains of a dead titan or god.

Chronepsis is the draconic god of fate and prophecy. It is also the name of a constellation in the skies of Eberron. The dragons who follow the faith of Thir worship Chronepsis among the pantheon of draconic deities. Dragons view him as having a role in either transcribing or deciding the path of the Prophecy, which is the subject to internal philosophical debate among dragons who follow Thir.

Corius Corralyn d'Sivis is a respected barrister of the Speakers Guild of House Sivis. Though he devotes most of his time to the law, he occasionally sells his services as an advocate, lobbying for clients or negotiating high-stakes legal agreements. Corius possesses the Mark of Scribing.
Dirge of Karrnath is a human weapons master from formerly part of the Laughing Knives residing in Stormreach in Xen'drik.
Dhulokk is a troglodyte spellcaster who dwells in the Waterworks beneath the city of Stormreach.
Dammerund is an elf illusionist and member of the gruesome and murderous Bloodborne Players theatrical troupe in Stormreach.

Eliri is an elven weaponmaster from Valenar. She taught a young Boranel ir'Wynarn of Breland how to ride and fight from the saddle. Boranel developed a youthful crush on her, the first love of his life, but he put his infatuation aside when he realized her age and his position meant he could not indulge it freely.
Erdis Cai is a vampire and a servant of the Blood of Vol. He was previously an adventurer and pirate.

Garblers are extraplanar aberrations that are commonly found in ancient libraries or underground in Xen'drik where they can read about magic. They come from the Realm of Madness, the plane of Xoriat. They use truename magic. The reason they are often found in libraries is because they are looking to expand their knowledge of truename magic. Although they are small solitary creatures, garblers are very powerful and aggressive aberrations.
Drego Sarhain is a Thranish human sorcerer and follower of the Silver Flame, and an active spy for his country.
Eldrantulku the Oathbreaker is an Overlord from the Age of Demons with dominion over corruption.
Dream serpents, or qulashtaq to the drow, are large, magical creatures native to the jungles and warm forests of Xen'drik, named for the hallucinatory effects of their venom.
Eva is a changeling living in Sharn, Breland. She works as an assistant, receptionist, and secretary for Ot at the Champion Inquisitive Agency.
Eclesta Xillian is a diviner and scholar of the Twelve based in Stormreach, Xen'drik.

Jabra is a night hag said to be a distant cousin of the Daughters of Sora Kell. She is an extremely skilled alchemist that owns a small tent-based shop in the city of Graywall, in the Daughters' nation of Droaam. In addition to selling traditional potions, she also produces unusual and possibly dangerous elixirs. It is said she has the ability to bottle the dreams and nightmares of an individual, which she then sells for a pretty penny.

Mind flayers, also called illithids, are evil and sadistic aberrations that feast on the minds of humanoids. They are considered the chief servants of the daelkyr, particularly Dyrrn the Corruptor. Mind flayers are native to the plane of Xoriat, the Realm of Madness, but many are also present in the depths of Khyber. They consume their victims' very personality by extracting and devouring their brains while they are still alive.
Katashka the Gatekeeper is an Overlord of undeath from the Age of Demons.
Kaorti are evil outsiders known for their ability to transform living creatures into more of their own kind.
A gloom golem, also known as a Mabarak golem or a doomhowler, is a planar golem powered by woe and despair. They are made on the plane of Mabar, the Endless Night.
Hallorek the Black is a Cyran sorcerer and retired military officer now living in New Cyre in Breland. He is the last of Cyre's Sorcerer-Generals, but is believed to be dying.

Heirloom is a warforged wizard considered to be one of the heroes of Khorvaire for their service in the Last War. At some point in time, Heirloom was transported from Eberron to the world of Valhalla, where they serve under the general Vydar. They were known to have learned mage hand and force orb and would use these spells in battle.

Gornath the Madwyrm is a mad psionic red dragon who is a threat across the length of Sarlona. He leads a cabal of rogue dragons in Sarlona and has a cult of yuan-ti devoted to his service known as the Gornatha.
Viceroy Kurn d'Velderan is a human dragonmark heir and the leader of House Tharashk operations in and around the city of Stormreach.
Sul Khatesh, called the Keeper of Secrets is an Overlord of occult knowledge from the Age of Demons.
Dietrich is a playable character and a Flame Lord of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. He possesses a Crest of Lamine, known in Dagda as the Diadem of the Endless.

Etzel is a Sorcerer and is one of the exclusive characters in Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and Fire Emblem: New Mystery of the Emblem. He is a wandering spell slinger that got caught in during the War of Shadows. He had a wife named Ursula, who died in one of many attacks that Dolhr launched, and all that is left of her is her ring he holds as a memento.
Epimenides is the overarching antagonist of Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes. He is the creator of Arval.
Fianna is a playable character from Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. She possesses a Diadem of Revival.

Forneus is a background character in Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia. He was an alchemist responsible for the existence of Grima and the Risen from Fire Emblem Awakening. His escapades are detailed in the Thabes Labyrinth.

Gwenchaos is the main antagonist of TearRing Saga: Utna Heroes Saga. He is the leader of the Gerxel Church and seeks to resurrect the dark dragon, Gerxel, through a ritual that requires the four shamans (Enteh, Katri, Tia, and Neyfa) as sacrifices. He was once the Sage of Earth, one of the Four Sages and finest students of the White Master Morse, but was cast out after he betrayed the others and unsealed the forbidden ★Zahhak spell. It is noteworthy that Gwenchaos is never fought by the player when he's human, although he does have scripted fights with Ezenbah, Richard, and Tia.
Knoll is a playable character in Fire Emblem: The Sacred Stones. He is one of Grado's royal mages who aided Lyon in his research into the Sacred Stones in an attempt to resurrect Emperor Vigarde.

Letizia is an antagonist introduced in Book VI of Fire Emblem Heroes. She is a member of the Imperial Royal Family of Embla, being ninth in line to the throne, and therefore has some blood relation to Veronica and Bruno. She also commands the Curse Directive, Embla's alternative to the Order of Heroes in Askr, which specializes in researching the dark arts.

Meshua is a backstory character in Fire Emblem: Radiant Dawn. She was the first Empress of Begnion and the daughter of Altina. Under her rule, Begnion was established as an empire and ruled all of Tellius, barring the region of Goldoa, in the name of the Goddess' chosen one. Like all Apostles before and after her (including her own daughter Yoram), Meshua was secretly a Branded of Heron descent. es:Meshua

Mahoba is an enemy character from TearRing Saga: Utna Heroes Saga. He is a member of the Gerxel Church who is known as the Demon Summoner. He criticizes Barbaross and reminds him of Silva's "betrayal" of Canaan in an attempt to make him feel ashamed.

Mikhail is an enemy boss character in Fire Emblem Gaiden and its remake, Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia. He is a priest of the Duma Faithful who guards the Temple of Mila. He uses Conjure to summon powerful gargoyles.
Sylwiss is a playable character from TearRing Saga: Berwick Saga. She is a master sniper who claims that she always kills whatever she aims at, though she is prone to exaggerating her prowess.

The Umbral Beast is an enemy-only class introduced in Fire Emblem: Three Houses. It is the result of Aelfric attempting to perform an incomplete Rite of Rising in order to revive Sitri, only to fuse with her body instead. The Chalice of Beginnings absorbed the blood drained from the descendants of the Four Apostles, turning it into a dangerous weapon which it uses against its enemies.

The Wight is an enemy-only Monster class that first debuts in Fire Emblem Gaiden. Reanimated skeletal corpses, usually of humans, driven by terrible magic, Wights, like their unpromoted counterparts, are capable of wielding a variety of weapons, including Swords, Lances and Bows. Wights are designed with a few ripped and tattered pieces of cloth draped over their skeletal bodies, most likely relics from their time as members of the living realm.
Viscount Essar is a character from Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes. He is a minor noble of the Adrestian Empire, and possesses a Minor Crest of Indech.
Zola is a non-playable character and a supporting antagonist in Fire Emblem Fates on all three routes. A mage of Nohr, he possesses the special ability to assume and alter the appearances of others.

|-|S5= =Season 5= Kevin the Cube is a Corruption Cube that first appeared in Season 5. It is a sentient being born from The Last Reality with malicious intent to corrupt everything. It is a major antagonist in Fortnite: Battle Royale, serving as the main antagonist of Season 5 and Season 6.
